The patient's phenotype — decreased IgM, decreased IgA, decreased total B cells, reduced NK cells, decreased class-switched memory B cells, recurrent viral/bacterial/fungal infections, chronic diarrhea — is classic for MALT1 deficiency (an immunodeficiency with combined B and NK cell defects, hypogammaglobulinemia, and susceptibility to bacterial, viral, and candidal infections). MALT1 is a well-established primary immunodeficiency gene causing this exact constellation. None of the evidence chunks directly name any gene as causal, but using prior knowledge of gene-disease associations, MALT1 is the strongest match. The phenotype does not fit MT-ATP8 (mitochondrial), IMPA2 (inositol metabolism), or the other candidates which have no known immunodeficiency associations matching this profile.
